idiom_name: discriminated union of object types + never-based exhaustiveness
implementation_notes: TypeScript encodes a sum type as a union of object types that share a literal discriminant property; narrowing on that property gives each branch its exact payload type, and a default branch typed as never (or an assertNever helper) turns a missing variant into a compile error. Products are interfaces or type literals, and readonly members plus as-const factories supply immutability. The union exists only in the type system - it is erased at run time - so the tag is an ordinary property and nothing validates untrusted input before narrowing.
pitfalls: The discriminant must be a literal type in every member; one member typed kind: string degrades the union so narrowing stops eliminating branches.
Discriminated unions are erased at run time, so JSON data is unchecked - a value decoded from the wire can carry an unknown kind and reach the default arm only at run time.
Excess property checks apply to fresh object literals only; a value assigned through an intermediate variable can carry extra fields without complaint.
An any or unknown member in the union makes the never-exhaustiveness check pass unconditionally, hiding a missing case.
